messages:
Alex C: Morning — noticed a perf regression on mixtral-moE after last runtime push. p50 stable, p99 jumped 420ms -> 1.2s for ~1k token sequences. Router logs show long tail in routing decision and many expert cache evictions. cc @Maria G

deploy-bot: Deployed "runtime/2026-03-16" to prod at 07:09 UTC :rocket:

Maria G: Oof. Can you paste profiler output and router metrics? top_k, gate temperature, expert_parallelism?

Alex C: Pasted profiling snippet:

```
Profiler summary (nvprof):
kernel: fast_attn_rope  65%  avg 0.9ms
kernel: generic_attention 25% avg 4.6ms
router_decision_cpu   8% avg 12ms
KV_cache_eviction task: spikes at 07:10
```

Router config excerpt:
```
router.top_k=4
router.temperature=1.0
experts.per_gpu=16
expert_parallelism=1
```

Kevin L: Two immediate suspects: top_k=4 is increasing router cost (softmax over more experts) and topk selection kernel may fallback to CPU path for large batch shapes. Try top_k=2 for canary. Also check gating logits scale — if logits are near-zero float issues cause extra ops.

Sophie R: Also looks like expert cache pressure — eviction rate jumped. KV cache hit rate dropped. Metrics:
```
expert_cache_hit_rate: 0.41
expert_cache_evictions_total: 13602
avg_kv_cache_size: 78MB
```

Maria G: For Mixtral MoE we saw RoPE scaling changes earlier that made some attention kernels choose slower fallback. Sequence len distribution changed -> different kernel selected. You can force kernel choice for experiment with `REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=attn_rope_fast` in runtime env. Also try `router.threshold=0.0001` to stabilize small logits.

Alex C: If we reduce top_k to 2, how much quality drop at eval? I can run A/B with the eval harness.

Kevin L: Another knob: expert_parallelism>1 spreads expert compute across devices and reduces per-device hot experts, but increases cross-device comm. For our infra the cross-comm is cheaper if it prevents cache thrash. Try expert_parallelism=2 in canary.

perf-bot: Profiler trace uploaded: https://internal.prod/perf/1756123456/trace.html (flamegraph + kernel timeline)

Sophie R: From trace: router decision time correlates with batches that have many unique routing destinations -> load imbalance. Consider top_k routing or capacity factor changes. Also batching heuristics: current max_batch_tokens=2048; when requests have long prefix KV hits decrease; set max_batch_tokens=1024 for long sequences to avoid huge all-to-all router work.

Maria G: Action plan:
- Canary 1: top_k=2, router.temperature=0.8, expert_parallelism=1, force fast attn kernel
- Canary 2: top_k=2, expert_parallelism=2, batching max_batch_tokens=1024
- Collect: p50/p90/p99, expert_cache_hit_rate, router_decision_time, kernel selection histogram

Alex C: Starting Canary 1 now. Will post metrics in 15m.

Kevin L: If Canary 1 reduces p99 but quality drops >1% on eval set, revert and try Canary 2.

Alex C: Canary 1 results (15m): p99 down to 540ms, cache_hit_rate up to 0.63, minor n-answer drift 0.6% on eval. Rolling to 10% traffic for Canary 2.

Sophie R: Nice. Keep an eye on GPU memory for expert_parallelism=2 — may push OOM on smaller instances.

Maria G: Great. Add telemetry for kernel fallback count and router softmax ops per batch so next time we detect early.

Alex C: Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
